issues.description: The problem statement (Part 2) refers to a method named getFeedingSound(), but the UML, tasks, template, and solution use/messageOnFeed() as the abstract feeding method. This inconsistent method name in the specification can confuse students about which method to implement and call when producing feeding sounds for animals.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: replace all references to getFeedingSound() in problem_statement.md with messageOnFeed() (and clarify return type String). Alternatively, explicitly state that getFeedingSound() and messageOnFeed() are the same and provide the canonical method name students should implement (preferably messageOnFeed()).

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the same feeding-sound method using two different identifiers: messageOnFeed() (UML and tasks) and getFeedingSound() (task descriptions and verse placeholders). The solution implements an abstract method named messageOnFeed() and all concrete animals implement messageOnFeed(), while the problem text and example verse use getFeedingSound(). This mismatch can confuse students about which method name to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement and verse placeholders with messageOnFeed(), or alternatively rename the abstract method in the solution/template to getFeedingSound() so the problem text and code use the same identifier. Ensure examples and instructions consistently reference the chosen name.
